blocks.title: Identity Lifecycle, Federation, and SSO comparison
Identity Lifecycle, Federation, and SSO exam shortcuts
items: New employee starts → PROVISION
Create the account and assign only required access.
Example: HR triggers creation of email and application accounts.
Employee leaves → DE-PROVISION
Disable accounts and revoke access promptly.
Example: A terminated user's VPN and SaaS access are removed.
Need to verify real-world identity → IDENTITY PROOFING
Confirm the person before issuing credentials.
Example: Verify government ID before account activation.
One login for many enterprise apps → SSO
Authenticate once, then reuse that session for authorized services.
Example: One corporate login opens several SaaS apps.
Partner organization uses its own identity provider → FEDERATION
Establish trust between separate identity domains.
Example: A supplier signs in with its own corporate identity.
App needs delegated access without user's password → OAUTH
Use authorization tokens rather than sharing credentials.
Example: A calendar app receives permission to read events.
Browser-based enterprise federation → SAML
SAML commonly carries identity assertions between IdP and service provider.
Example: Corporate IdP sends a SAML assertion to a SaaS app.
blocks.example: First determine whether the scenario is asking who the user is, what they can do, how they authenticate, or how privileged access should be controlled.

questions.q: A new employee needs an email account and access to approved business applications. Which IAM activity is this?
questions.explanation: Provisioning creates accounts and assigns required access.

questions.q: An employee leaves the company and all accounts and remote access must be disabled. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: De-provisioning removes accounts and access that are no longer needed.

questions.q: Before creating an account, HR verifies a person's government-issued identification. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Identity proofing confirms that the person is who they claim to be.

questions.q: A user authenticates once and then accesses several authorized SaaS applications without signing in again. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: SSO allows one authentication event to provide access to multiple authorized applications.

questions.q: A supplier logs in to your application using the supplier's own identity provider. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Federation establishes trust between separate identity domains.

questions.q: An application receives permission to access a user's calendar without receiving the user's password. Which protocol/framework is most relevant?
questions.explanation: OAuth supports delegated authorization using tokens rather than sharing the user's password.

questions.q: A browser-based enterprise SSO solution passes identity assertions from an identity provider to a cloud application. Which standard is most likely used?
questions.explanation: SAML is commonly used for browser-based federation and SSO assertions.

questions.q: Managers review employee permissions every quarter and certify that access is still appropriate. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Attestation is a formal review or certification that access remains appropriate.
